questions.title: How does Double Quantization specifically reduce memory footprint compared to storing 4-bit constants, and is there a theoretical upper bound on this savings?
questions.question_body: The paper states that Double Quantization quantizes the quantization constants ($c_2$), reducing memory from 0.5 bits per parameter to approximately 0.127 bits per parameter. However, I am confused about how they claim this saves approximately 3 GB for a 65B model if the calculation $(32/64) - (8/64 + ...) = 0.373$. If I naively calculate $65 * 10^9 * 0.373$, that equals roughly 24 GB, not 3 GB. Am I misunderstanding the bit-per-parameter units or calculating it incorrectly?

questions.title: Why does GRU/LSTM not apply to standard LoRA implementation, and what makes active LoRA compatible with standard GRU layers
questions.question_body: I'm trying to understand why active LoRA works with any linear layer but might not be universally applicable to regions of neural networks like attention heads.

questions.title: Can you explain why using REFRESH token instead of special tokens like EOS is crucial for handling long texts?
questions.question_body: In standard implementations of PaLM tokenization, special tokens like EOS are used to mark end-of-sequence boundaries. In April, they removed these special tokens and replaced them with REFRESH token which is just a space character ' '.
